title: Connectivity via edges crossing every vertex bipartition
statement: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite, nonempty vertex set $V$. Then $G$ is connected if and only if, for every set $S \subseteq V$ such that both $S$ and its complement $V \setminus S$ are nonempty, there exist vertices $u \in S$ and $v \in V \setminus S$ that are adjacent in $G$.
